ambiguity_notes: Quote is the portion of the sentence after the folio-125 page break; the full sentence reads 'the planets who are in association with / the lord of the 2nd are the most powerful in causing death' (opening clause quoted in raman.hpa.xv.occupants_of_second_stronger_than_lord). Ranking convention; proposed impl: conjunct_lord_of(planet, house).

consequent.text: Planets in association with the lord of the 2nd are the most powerful in causing death.

quote: the lord of the 2nd are the most powerful in causing death.

ambiguity_notes: Hyphenated line break 'con- join' joined per guide. Requires functional malefic-ness ('become evil'), Yogakaraka status, conjunction with the death-house lords and the prior non-occurrence of primary maraka dasas - none expressible in the DSL (proposed impls: is_yogakaraka(planet), conjunct_lord_of(planet, house)).

consequent.text: When the periods of the occupants or owners of the death houses do not come in time, death may occur in the dasas of planets that are not Yogakarakas but become evil and conjoin the lords of the death houses.

timing.detail: Death in the dasas of non-Yogakaraka planets which become evil and conjoin the lords of the 2nd and 7th, when the periods of the occupants/owners of the death houses do not come in time.

quote: If the periods of the planets occupying or owning death houses do not come in time, then death may occur in the dasas of planets who are not Yogokarakas but who become evil and conjoin lords of the houses of death.

ambiguity_notes: Nomenclature; no testable chart condition. Mirrors the DSL house group 'maraka' = (2, 7).

consequent.text: The 2nd and 7th houses are the houses of death (maraka sthanas).

quote: The 7th house and the 2nd house are called houses of death.

ambiguity_notes: Nomenclature; no testable chart condition. OCR 'arc' (for 'are') preserved verbatim.

consequent.text: The 8th house from lagna and the 8th from the 8th (the 3rd from lagna) are the houses of life.

quote: The 8th house from lagna (ascendant) and the 8th from that, i.e., the 3rd from lagna arc termed as houses of life.

ambiguity_notes: Conjunction with the lord of the 12th is not expressible (planets_conjunct takes concrete names only; proposed impl: conjunct_lord_of(planet, house)), and the antecedent also requires the failure of the three primary maraka classes. 'if he is the lord of the 3rd or 8th house' read as qualifying the papa bhukti-lord.

consequent.text: Failing marakas of the three primary classes, the planet conjoined with the lord of the 12th - even a benefic - causes death in its dasa, in the bhukthi of a malefic who is lord of the 3rd or 8th.

timing.detail: Death in the dasa of the planet conjoined with the lord of the 12th, during the bhukthi of a malefic who is lord of the 3rd or 8th house.

quote: If marakas cannot be found out of these three, then the planet in conjunction with the lord of 12th, even if it is a benefic, causes death in his dasa (period) in the bhukthi (sub-period) of a papa (malefic) if he is the lord of the 3rd or 8th house.

ambiguity_notes: Needs a strongest-of comparison among the specific house lords and the non-occurrence of a prior dasa within the life-term - neither expressible in the DSL (proposed impl: strongest_lord_of(houses)). Note the preceding sentence conditions on the planet conjoined with the 12th lord, while this one speaks of the 12th lord's own dasa - Raman's cascade is quoted as printed.

consequent.text: If the dasa of the lord of the 12th (Vyayadhipathi) does not come, the most powerful among the lords of the 3rd, 6th and 8th becomes the maraka.

timing.detail: Death in the dasa of the most powerful among the lords of the 3rd, 6th and 8th, when the dasa of the lord of the 12th does not operate.

quote: If the dasa of Vyayadhipathi (lord of the 12th) does not come then one most powerful among the lords of the 3rd, 6th and 8th becomes maraka.

ambiguity_notes: OCR heavily garbled - intended reading 'Lords of 3 and 8 are also probable causers of death'; quoted verbatim with 'are 8 ate', 'dekth' and 'etc,,'. Fallback ordering over prior dasa non-occurrence is not a chart predicate.

consequent.text: The lords of the 3rd and 8th are also probable causers of death if death does not occur in the dasas mentioned in item 4.

timing.detail: Dasas of the lords of the 3rd and 8th, as the next resort after item 4 of the summary.

quote: Lords of 3 are 8 ate also probable causers of dekth if death does not occur in the dasas, etc,, mentioned in item 4.

ambiguity_notes: Requires the ayurdaya classification (short/middle/long life) and the dasha timeline mapped against the life-term boundary - data/comparison outside the chart-predicate DSL. OCR 'malicious,one' preserved. Proposed impl: maraka_dasha_within_ayurdaya_term.

consequent.text: A weaker maraka whose dasa falls within the allotted span of life kills in preference to the most powerful maraka whose dasa operates only after that span.

timing.detail: The maraka dasa that operates within the years allotted to the indicated life-term (e.g. Madhyayu) brings death, in preference to a more malicious maraka whose dasa falls outside that term.

quote: Suppose, a horoscope indicates middle life or Madhyayu whereas the dasa of a most powerful maraka comes into operation after 80 years. In such a circumstance the period of a planet, no matter even if it is less malicious in causing death which comes within the maximum number of years allotted for Madhyayu, must be determined as bringing about death, in preference to the most malicious,one.

ambiguity_notes: Definitional; 'generally' hedges the timing claim. OCR drop-cap artifact 'ARAKAS ... A of inflicting' preserved verbatim (reads 'MARAKAS are planets possessed of the power of inflicting death'). Maraka membership itself is enumerated in raman.hpa.xv.maraka_planets_enumeration. Proposed impl: is_maraka(planet).

consequent.text: Marakas are planets possessed of the power of inflicting death; death generally occurs during their periods and sub-periods.

timing.detail: Death generally occurs during the periods (dasas) and sub-periods (bhuktis) of maraka planets.

quote: ARAKAS are planets possessed of the power A of inflicting death. Death generally occurs during the periods and sub-periods of such planets.

ambiguity_notes: Per-planet role assignment, not a chart-level predicate; the DSL has no planet-scoped classification form (proposed impl: is_maraka(planet)). Summary items 1-3 on p.126 restate this enumeration verbatim in list form; item 3 clarifies that the conjunction class comprises planets neither owning nor occupying the 2nd/7th - folded here rather than duplicated.

consequent.text: The maraka planets are: the lords of the 2nd and 7th, the occupants of the 2nd and 7th, and the planets in conjunction with those lords.

quote: Thus the lords of the 2nd and the 7th, their occupants and the planets who are in conjunction with them are the Maraka planets.

ambiguity_notes: Procedural instruction (order of operations for death prediction), not a chart predicate; needs ayurdaya determination which the DSL does not carry.

consequent.text: Procedure: first ascertain whether the horoscope indicates short, middle or long life; then determine the maraka planets and the times their influences fructify.

quote: Ascertain beforehand, whether a horoscope indicates short, middle or long life - determine the maraka planets and the times when their influences will come to fruition.

ambiguity_notes: 'Most malicious planet in the horoscope' is a superlative over functional and natural malefic-ness with no DSL form (proposed impl: most_malicious_planet), and the condition requires whole-timeline dasa non-occurrence.

consequent.text: If no maraka dasa ever comes into operation, the most malicious planet in the horoscope will cause death.

timing.detail: Dasa of the most malicious planet in the horoscope, when no maraka dasa operates at all within the span of life.

quote: If the dasa of a death-inflicting planet does not at all come into operation, then the most malicious planet in the horoscope will cause death.

ambiguity_notes: Ranking convention among maraka candidates. The sentence continues across the printed page break (folio 125): '...and the planets who are in association with | the lord of the 2nd are the most powerful in causing death' - the continuation is recorded separately in raman.hpa.xv.associates_of_second_lord_most_powerful.

consequent.text: In maraka power, occupants of the 2nd house outrank its lord.

quote: Planets who occupy the 2nd are stronger than the planets who own it, intending to cause death

ambiguity_notes: Hyphenated line break 'con- junction' joined per guide. Saturn conjunct the lord of the 2nd/7th is not expressible (proposed impl: conjunct_lord_of(planet, house)). The dasha timing is inferred from the chapter context, not stated in this sentence.

consequent.text: Saturn, made evil by conjunction with the lords of the death houses, causes death in preference to any of those lords.

timing.detail: Saturn's period takes precedence in inflicting death over the death-house lords he joins (dasha mode inferred from the chapter's frame that marakas kill in their periods).

quote: Saturn, inclined to produce evil by his conjunction with the lords of death houses, will cause death in preference to any of those planets.

ambiguity_notes: Longitude arithmetic and Saturn transit cycles are outside the DSL (occupies_khara/chidra cover other points only; proposed impl: saturn_transit_death_point) and the rule needs the ayurdaya classification. OCR 'In the ease of' (for 'case') preserved.

consequent.text: Death occurs when Saturn transits the zodiacal point given by the sum of the longitudes of Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun and the Moon, in his first, second or third cycle according as the life is short, middle or long.

timing.detail: Death when Saturn transits the point formed by adding the longitudes of Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun and the Moon (expunging multiples of 12 signs): in his first cycle for short life, second for middle life, third for long life.

quote: Add together the longitudes of Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun and the Moon. This gives us a point in the zodiac after expunging multiples of 12. In the ease of short, middle and long life, death occurs when Saturn transits over this point, in his first, second and third cycles respectively.

ambiguity_notes: Precedence ordering between the death houses; a ranking convention, not a per-chart predicate.

consequent.text: Between the two death houses, the 2nd is always stronger in inflicting death than the 7th.

quote: The 2nd house is always stronger in inflicting death than the 7th.

ambiguity_notes: Read distributively (either luminary qualifying by either route): no lagna gives Sun and Venus jointly the 2nd and 7th lordships, so the joint reading is vacuous. Encoded as a disjunction over Sun/Venus lordship of 2, 7 or a kendra (1, 4, 10; 7 already listed); the antecedent fires chart-wide and loses the per-planet attribution of maraka-hood, hence partial.

consequent.text: The Sun and Venus are sure to become marakas when they own the 2nd or 7th or obtain Kendradhipatya (lordship of a quadrant).

quote: If the Sun and Sukra (Venus) are lords of the 2nd and 7th or get Kendradhipatya (lordship of quadrant)— they are sure to become marakas.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Aquarius lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Venus alone is auspicious. The combination of Venus and Mars causes Rajayoga. Jupiter and the Moon are evil.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Aries lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Saturn, Mercury and Venus are ill-disposed. Jupiter and the Sun are auspicious. The mere combination of Jupiter and Saturn produces no beneficial results. Jupiter is the Yogakaraka or the planet producing success. If Venus becomes a Maraka he will not kill the native but planets like Saturn will bring about death to the person.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Cancer lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Venus and Mercury are evil. Jupiter and Mars give beneficial results. Mars is the Rajayogakamka (conferer of name and fame). The combination of Mars and Jupiter also causes Rajayoga (combination for political success). The Sun does not kill the person although possessed of Maraka powers. Venus and other inauspicious planets kill the native.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Capricorn lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Venus is the most powerful planet and in conjunction with Mercury produces Rajayoga. Mars, Jupiter and the Moon are evil.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Gemini lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Mars, Jupiter and the Sun are evil. Venus alone is most beneficial and in conjunction with Saturn in good signs produces an excellent career of much fame. Combination of Saturn and Jupiter produces similar results as in Aries* Venus and Mercury when well associated cause Rajayoga. The Moon will not kill the person even though possessed of death-inflicting powers*

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Leo lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: conjunction of Jupiter and Mars in favourable houses produce Rajayoga. Saturn, Venus and Mercury are evil. Saturn does not kill the native when he has the Maraka power but Mercury and other evil planets inflict death when they get Maraka powers.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Libra lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Saturn alone causes Rajayoga. Jupiter, the Sun and Mars are inauspicious. Mercury and Saturn produce good. The conjunction of the Moon and Mercury produce Rajayoga. Mars himself will not kill the person. Jupiter, Venus and Mars when possessed of Maraka powers certainly kill the native.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Pisces lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: The Moon and Mars are auspicious. Mars is most powerful. Mars with the Moon or Jupiter causes Rajayoga. Saturn, Venus, the Sun and Mercury are evil. Mars himself does not kill the person even if he is a Maraka.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Sagittarius lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Mars is the best planet and in conjunction with Jupiter produces much good- The Sun and Mars also produce good. Venus is evil. When the Sun and Mars combine together they produce Rajayoga. Saturn does not bring about death even when he is a Maraka. But Venus causes death when he gets jurisdiction as a Maraka planet.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Scorpio lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Jupiter is beneficial. The Sun and the Moon produce Rajayoga. Mercury and Venus are evil. Jupiter, even if he becomes a Maraka does not inflict death.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Taurus lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Saturn is the most auspicious and powerful planet. Jupiter, Venus and the Moon are evil planets. Saturn alone produces Rajayoga.

consequent.text: Key-planet roles for Virgo lagna: functional benefic/malefic, Rajayoga-producing and Maraka behaviour per Raman.

quote: Venus alone is most powerful. Mercury and Venus when combined together cause Rajayoga. Mars and the Moon are evil. The Sun does not kill the native even if he becomes a Maraka but Venus, the Moon and Jupiter will inflict death when they are possessed of death-inflicting power.
